trace: GraphRecord stores full content plus identity, Provenance(path, sha256, locator, verified), trust, sensitivity, freshness, admission, eligibility, agent origin, export_allowed, tags, and sequence.

Public export uses export_graph. It is default-deny, requires explicit policy, requested identities, export_allowed, authenticated eligibility, allowed sensitivity, and complete edge endpoints. It emits graph-export-v1 with metadata-only record pointers; content is omitted.

serialize_projection emits graph-projection-v1. It orders selected records by topology, emits metadata-only pointers and retained edges, and prunes records from the end until byte_budget fits. A fail-closed selection emits no records or edges.

Source-backed context is a separate path. select_documents and select_context may include exact source content only after provenance, source snapshot, UTF-8, and excerpt/full-record equality checks. Default TaskSpec sensitivity is public.
answer.privacy_boundary: GraphRecord.to_dict retains content, but public export and serialized projection call to_pointer_dict, which excludes content. Restricted or otherwise unauthenticated records cannot enter those outputs. The Orcastrata adapter maps records as trust=unverifiable, freshness=unknown, eligible=false, export_allowed=false, and always requires direct fallback.
answer.preserved_evidence: Exports preserve record identity, title, provenance path/hash/locator/verification, trust, sensitivity, freshness, admission, eligibility, agent_generated, export_allowed, tags, sequence, and edge provenance. Source-backed projections preserve source_path, source_sha256, byte ranges or full content, and excerpt hashes. Catalog intake preserves producer evidence_state, provenance, sensitivity, exportability, tag owner/source, projection/graph/board/raw-receipt digests, and canonical owner references.
answer.budget_behavior: TaskSpec enforces positive node and byte budgets. Selection limits nodes and depth. Serialized projections prune optional records to byte_budget; fail-closed envelopes must also fit or raise. Source-backed document/context projections fail closed when required content exceeds byte_budget. Explicit fallback uses only caller-declared paths and remaining budget.
answer.canonical_ownership: Repository source remains canonical and the graph is a derived navigation view. GoalBuddy owns lifecycle and acceptance truth; WorkGraph owns dependency, readiness, scope, validation, and evidence truth; VelGraphing owns consumer admission and graph mapping; GitHub is only a synchronized collaboration surface. Generated plugin runtime files are projections of canonical package sources.
answer.package_drift_checks: The parity verifier validates projection-map shape, safe boundaries, unique mappings, approved exclusions, source/runtime byte equality, exact runtime file sets, projection-state contract identity and file digests, release-manifest inventory, package identity, and candidate digest. Current read-only parity passed with candidate_sha256 a7e6cdfed136c208a3009eb945c255139bacaf0e011b4f0093f67ff461f77e0b and 74 files.
answer.limits: The adapter's graph mapping is navigation-only and does not authenticate underlying WorkGraph or GoalBuddy state. Parity proves source/package consistency only; it does not prove installation, publication, federation, provider execution, or adoption.
